name: Question 3
problem:
The Taylor series for the function $f(x)$ about $x=2$ is given by

$$
f(x)={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n}}{(2n-1)!}(x-2)^{2n}.
$$

Calculate the first three non-zero terms of the Taylor series expansion about $x=2$ of ${f}^{′}(x).$
worked_solution:
Writing the first few terms of the series explicitly, we have

$$
f(x)={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n}}{(2n-1)!}(x-2)^{2n}=-(x-2)^{2}+\frac{1}{6}(x-2)^{4}-\frac{1}{120}(x-2)^{6}+⋯.
$$

To find ${f}^{′}(x),$ we differentiate term-by-term. This gives

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=-2(x-2)+\frac{2}{3}(x-2)^{3}-\frac{1}{20}(x-2)^{5}+⋯.
$$

Question 3
?

The Taylor series for the function f(x) about x=2 is given by f(x)=∑n=1∞(−1)n(2n−1)!(x−2)2n. Calculate the first three non-zero terms of the Taylor series expansion about x=2 of f′(x).

a
f′(x)=−(x−2)+13(x−2)3−19(x−2)5+⋯
b
f′(x)=−2(x−2)+15(x−2)3−120(x−2)5+⋯
c
f′(x)=−(x−2)+14(x−2)3−19(x−2)5+⋯
d
f′(x)=−2(x−2)+23(x−2)3−49(x−2)5+⋯
e
f′(x)=−2(x−2)+23(x−2)3−120(x−2)5+⋯
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Writing the first few terms of the series explicitly, we have f(x)=∑n=1∞(−1)n(2n−1)!(x−2)2n=−(x−2)2+16(x−2)4−1120(x−2)6+⋯.

To find f′(x), we differentiate term-by-term. This gives f′(x)=−2(x−2)+23(x−2)3−120(x−2)5+⋯.
